idiom_name: discriminated union + typed handler registry with runtime validation (zod)
implementation_notes: TypeScript erases types, so the command base is a discriminated union (`{ kind: "render"; reportId: number } | ...`) serialised as JSON and the invoker is a handler registry typed as `Record<Command["kind"], Handler>` or an exhaustive `switch` whose default is a `never` check - the compiler keeps the registry complete and the runtime keeps the payload honest. Because the wire value is not the compile-time type, the envelope must be validated at the boundary: `z.discriminatedUnion("kind", ...)` gives the parser the tag-to-schema mapping, and only validated commands reach handlers. Classes with an execute() method are justified only for in-process commands; they are not what crosses the boundary.
pitfalls: Type assertions (`as Command`) or JSON.parse typed as any skip the runtime check, so a renamed field fails deep inside a handler instead of at the boundary; validate with a schema and dispatch on the validated tag.

JSON cannot carry undefined, Date, Map/Set, bigint or class identity, and keys such as __proto__ survive parsing as data: use Map or null-prototype lookups for registries and normalise dates and decimals explicitly.

Discriminated unions are compile-time only: handlers for a removed case linger unless the registry is typed from the union, and payloads from older deploys must be tolerated (version the envelope) rather than rejected outright.
